title: Hybrid NMR structure maps H-NS contacts with AT-rich DNA
summary: A solution NMR structure of an E. coli H-NS domain bound to AT-rich DNA revealed auxiliary linker contacts beside its established AT-hook-like recognition motif. Mutational and NMR analyses supported their cooperative contribution to DNA binding. TALOS-N neural-network predictions supplied protein dihedral restraints alongside experimental NMR/NOE measurements and structural refinement. This is a hybrid experimental/computational result; the study did not isolate the learned component’s contribution or establish independent replication.

evidence.tested: The solution structure calculation used experimentally measured NOE restraints and TALOS-N-derived protein dihedral restraints; 20 lowest-energy conformers were selected. Mutational and NMR titration analyses tested the proposed H-NS/DNA contact contributions.
evidence.unknown: The learned component was not isolated by ablation. An isolated domain/DNA complex does not establish the behavior of full-length oligomeric H-NS in cells; independent replication was not established.
evidence.ai_role: TALOS-N, an artificial-neural-network-based hybrid predictor, supplied protein dihedral-angle restraints used in the H-NS85–137/AT-rich-DNA solution structure calculation. The structural interpretation also depends on NMR/NOE measurements, mutational/NMR analyses and other structure-refinement steps.

source_review.scope: Source-provenanced publisher PDF abstract, solution-structure Methods2.4, structural result and discussion, bounded mutational/NMR result summary, affiliations and publication date; original NIH TALOS-N developer documentation for its ANN operation. No experimental reproduction.
